question.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ Every real $2\times 2$ matrix is not singular.
question.worked_solution:
Let ${M}_{2}(R)$ be the set of all real $2\times 2$ matrices. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ For all $x\in {M}_{2}(R),$ $x$ is not singular.

Introducing the universal quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∀x\in {M}_{2}(R),\,x\text{ is not singular}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀x\in {M}_{2}(R),\,x\text{ is not singular}) & ≡∃x\in {M}_{2}(R),\,¬(x\text{ is not singular}) \\  & ≡∃x\in {M}_{2}(R),\,x\text{ is singular}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ There exists $x\in {M}_{2}(R)$ such that $x$ is singular.

or simply

$\,$ Some real $2\times 2$ matrices are singular.

choices.value: Some real $2\times 2$ matrices are not singular.
